vocab.definition: a graph of energy against progress of reaction.
the minimum energy needed to start a reaction.
the difference between reactant and product energy.

misconceptions.wrong: Activation energy is the same as ΔH.
misconceptions.right: Eₐ is the hump; ΔH is the start-to-end change.
A catalyst lowers Eₐ but ΔH is unchanged.
Exothermic products end LOWER than reactants.

infoPanels.title: EXOTHERMIC PROFILE
infoPanels.secondaryContent: The peak shows Eₐ; the drop shows energy released.

questions.text: On a profile, state what the peak and the overall drop represent. [2 marks]
State what is meant by activation energy. [1 mark]
Explain how a profile shows that a reaction is exothermic. [2 marks]
Explain how a catalyst changes the profile. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: A catalyst provides a route with a ______ ______ energy.

questions.text: Sketch the profile of an endothermic reaction with its Eₐ. [3 marks]

footer.tip: Eₐ = the hump to climb. ΔH = the height difference start to end.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does lowering Eₐ speed up a reaction without changing the energy released?
